messages:
Mira: heads up — nightly eval flagged a noticeable drop on pset-42 after the promptbank merge yesterday. link: https://github.com/redwood/promptbank/pull/432 :warning:
nightly-bot: [AUTO] nightly eval 2026-03-19: pset-42 intent_f1 -4.5% vs baseline, failing cases +12% (summary attached)
Mira: the PR reordered several negative examples and applied a small normalization. suspect label flips on some prompts.
Sami: can you paste the minimal diff that changed ordering/normalization?
Chen: here—small excerpt:
```diff
-  - input: "no, don't do X"
-    label: NEG
+  - input: "do not do X"  # normalization applied
+    label: NEG
```
Chen: but the canonical negative pool was also shuffled relative to the prompt indices, so some prompts might now map to different negatives.
Mira: repro attached (short prompt + bad generation example). seems deterministic on the canary model.
Sami: starting a bisect on promptbank history + running local nightly on a canary replica. will report minimal failing set.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout for model redwood/v2-canary paused by regression policy (rule: nightly-delta > 2%)
Eva: do we know customer impact? which routes use pset-42 tests in prod?
Mira: pset-42 is used by hosted-chat QA checks and a couple of internal helpdesk automations — low traffic but visible when it breaks.
Chen: two options: revert the merge (fast) or update the label-mapping/normalization logic to preserve index-to-example alignment (safer).
Sami: prefer targeted revert for now to stop the regression signal. then we can roll forward with a mapping script and tests. opening revert PR.
Sami: opened https://github.com/redwood/promptbank/pull/435 — revert just the ordering change, canary-only for quick verification.
Mira: please add a post-merge checklist: unit test that asserts stable label assignments across normalizations + a note in the PR template. also run tokenization sanity because quantized models showed amplified flips last time.
nightly-bot: re-run scheduled for canary in 30m (auto-trigger) :clock1:
Chen: small follow-up — tokenization differences between quantized runtime and full-precision can amplify subtle wording changes; include tokenizer diff in the bisect.
Mira: ack. add tokenizer check to the bisect steps and to the rebaseline checklist.
Eva: thanks all — ping me once canary re-run completes, will update support doc if we need a rollback notice.
Sami: will post results in ~45m. if revert fixes it, we then prepare a careful re-introduction with mapping tests. :thumbsup:
